subject: NovaRetail: performance qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novaretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-08T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: SLOs, sample workloads, and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can qualify the performance/SLOs you shared.

Recap of what we heard from NovaRetail on the call:
- Primary use case: real-time product recommendation assistant embedded in mobile app (streaming responses preferred).
- Target latency: interactive feel — p95 per-request end-to-end target ~250ms (stream-first; earliest-token latency matter).
- Throughput & concurrency: expected peak steady-state concurrency ~40 simultaneous sessions, overall peak QPS ~120 requests/s during promotions.
- Token throughput: typical request = 180 tokens; expected aggregate token rate ~21.6k tokens/minute at peak.
- Availability/SLAs: prefer Dedicated capacity but ok to start on Hosted for qualification.

To make the benchmark replicable and useful for procurement:
1) We will hand over a focused prompt set and harness that reproduces your interactive streaming workload (short prompts + follow-ups).
2) Measurement definitions we propose: p50/p95/p99 latency for first-token and full-response; sustained throughput over a 5-minute window; warm vs cold start (warm = after 30s idle; cold = after 30m idle).
3) Test variants: single-zone (us-west) run, multi-zone fallback run, and a quantized model run (if you want to test cost/latency tradeoffs).
4) We need a 60–90 minute window next week where you can run test traffic from your side (we provide client harness) and we’ll run server-side metrics.

What I’m sending you next: a first-draft prompt set and a short harness readme. If this matches your expectations, please:
- Confirm the p95 target of ~250ms (streaming-first) or provide an alternate numeric SLO.
- Share any hard constraints (e.g., maximum tokens per request, allowed quantization/precision, required data residency).
- Suggest 2 possible 90-minute windows next week for a joint run.

No attachments in this note — I’ll upload the harness and prompt set once I get your confirmation on targets.

Thanks —
Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: SLOs, sample workloads, and next steps

Thanks, Karthik — that exactly matches what we discussed. A few clarifications and constraints from our side:

- SLOs: we can stretch p95 to 300ms if that materially improves token-cost, but prefer <=250ms for high-conversion flows. First-token latency is the most critical metric for UX.
- Concurrency: 40 simultaneous sessions is a good baseline; during promotions we may see short bursts up to 120 concurrent sessions. Please treat burst traffic as important for the run.
- Streaming: must support partial tokens as they generate (we use the earliest-token to render typing state).
- Security/datagovernance: production must be in us-west region; no customer PII in prompt logs for benchmark runs (we will scrub).

Procurement looped in for pricing/contract follow-ups. Security will need the SOC2 evidence pack and the network topology sketch if we move to Dedicated.

I'm attaching our workload sketch (workload-spec.xlsx) for reference — it includes session arrival patterns and token distributions.

Available windows next week for the joint run: Tue 2026-07-14 09:00–11:00 PT or Thu 2026-07-16 13:00–15:00 PT. Either works; we prefer Tuesday if possible.

Elena
Elena Ruiz
Director, Digital Products — NovaRetail
elena.ruiz@novaretail.com

Subject: RE: NovaRetail: performance qualification & benchmark methodology — internal plan

Looping internally to split work for the NovaRetail run. Summary of owners and immediate tasks: 

- Karthik: coordinate with Elena on the exact joint-run window (she prefers Tue 7/14 09:00 PT). Confirm test accounts and any IP allow-list requirements.
- Rishi: please prepare a trimmed SOC2 + network topology sketch for security and confirm what we can disclose for the Dedicated evaluation. Also note any hard limits on KMS/HSM for private deployments.
- Laura: own the benchmark harness repo and prompt set packaging. Deliverables:
  * prompt_set_v1.jsonl (150 prompts covering recommendations + follow-ups)
  * harness README with reproducible run steps, docker-compose for client-side load generator, and measurement definitions.

Measurement definitions to include in the harness README (Rishi/Laura to finalize):
- First-token latency: time from request receive to first token emitted (stream-first focus). Report p50/p95/p99.
- Full-response latency: time to completion for the final token. p50/p95/p99.
- Sustained throughput: measured as average tokens/sec and requests/sec across a 5-minute window at target concurrency.
- Cold start: defined as 30-minute idle -> first request measured.
- Concurrency definition: number of simultaneously active streaming connections that the server handles without queuing beyond 10ms per-request.

Checklist before Tue run:
- Elena to confirm window and provide an allow-list (IP ranges) if needed.
- Monica to provision temporary test keys and send to Elena by EOD 7/12.
- Laura to upload prompt_set_v1.jsonl and harness README to shared Drive by EOD 7/12.

I'll take notes during the run and coordinate a post-run report.

-Monica

Subject: Re: NovaRetail: performance qualification & benchmark methodology — harness & run details

Elena — thanks for confirming the Tue window. Per our internal alignment, attaching the first-pass artifacts for your review and for the joint run:

Attachments (stubs):
- novaretail-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (150 prompts, mixed-length, includes follow-up prompts and simulated session ids)
- novaretail-benchmark-harness-instructions.pdf (README + reproducible steps + Docker client for traffic generation)

Quick highlights from the harness README (please review):
- How to run: docker-compose up client-load-gen (we provide a client image that replays the prompt_set with realistic inter-message think times).
- Measurement endpoints: we expose per-request traces to our console (token timestamps, cpu/gpu counters). For the joint run we will share a live dashboard link and post-run CSVs.
- Reproducibility notes: include model checkpoint tag (redwood/model-x:2026-06-30), quantization flags (int8-llm, cross-layer-kernel set v3), fixed random seed for tokenizer sampling when testing deterministic variants.
- Warm vs cold protocol: harness enforces 30-minute idle to simulate cold starts and 2-minute idle for warm runs.

Measurement definitions (excerpt):
- First-token latency: request.t_first - request.t_recv; report p50/p95/p99.
- Full-response latency: request.t_last - request.t_recv; report p50/p95/p99.
- Sustained throughput: mean tokens/sec and requests/sec across the central 5-minute interval (drop first/last 30s to remove warmup/tear-down).
- Concurrency: number of simultaneous active streaming sockets. For the run we will sweep 10/20/40/80 concurrent streams and hold each level for 5 minutes.

Repro steps (short):
1) Confirm joint window (we have Tue 2026-07-14 09:00–11:00 PT on hold) — if you prefer Thu 7/16, tell us.
2) NovaRetail: provide allow-list IPs and a test account that can generate load (we'll provide client keys).
3) We will coordinate a 15-minute dry run, then the 60-minute measured sweep.

If everything looks good I’ll upload the artifacts to the shared Drive and send the client key via the secure channel. Want to be explicit about the fallback plan: if hosted capacity can't meet p95 250ms in the run, we will spin a Dedicated test pool (same model variant) and rerun within 48 hours.

Link to artifacts (internal): https://drive.google.com/novaretail/benchmark-harness

Please reply with a thumbs-up or any edits to measurement definitions by EOD 7/15.
